clue.text: The fashion in Bristol?

parts.note: read on the surface as clothing style, but it is the second half of a stock nautical phrase
the old port of Bristol gave its name to the phrase about everything being tidy and seaworthy

explanation.surface: A query about what people wear in the city of Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: The full idiom is 'shipshape and Bristol fashion', meaning neat and in good order; Bristol is a historic English port city.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pairs these two halves as equivalents, each meaning trim, orderly and ready for sea.

clue.text: Animal sluggishness

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the slow-moving tree-dwelling mammal of South America
second meaning: laziness, one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of a lazy creature; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the slow tree mammal and the vice of idleness, which the creature was named after.

clue.text: Little Edward, stricken with colic, was freezing

indicators.note: something stricken is afflicted and knocked out of shape, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
Ed is the short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A small boy called Edward, suffering from stomach pains, was shivering cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stricken with colic' reads as illness, but stricken is the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely chilly to the touch is described by this compound adjective.

clue.text: Appear, reportedly, at the junction

indicators.note: reportedly signals that we want a word heard rather than spelt, so a sound-alike is entered

parts.note: to seem is to appear to be

explanation.surface: Someone is said to show up at a crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces of material are joined together.

clue.text: Note: free but parched

parts.note: A is one of the musical notes
to rid is to free or clear of something

explanation.surface: A memo observing that something is no-cost yet dried out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe land or throats left completely dry, without moisture.

clue.text: The last one, of course

parts.note: the final item in a series, apparently said with resignation
read as 'naturally', it actually means 'belonging to a golf course'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' sounds like an aside but means of a golf course, whose standard round ends at hole number eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard golf course has eighteen holes, so the final hole played carries this ordinal.

clue.text: Stuff idiot had first

parts.note: clot is a British informal word for a fool

indicators.note: first here means only the opening letter of the word had is taken

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone saying a fool got there before them, with 'stuff' as a dismissive exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks as if it modifies 'had' in time, but it picks out a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven fabric or material, the same as this textile.

clue.text: Large beast found in valley of a Scottish river?

parts.note: the Clyde is the river flowing through Glasgow; 'of' gives the possessive form
a dale is a valley, especially in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A big animal discovered living in a Scottish glen.
explanation.walkthrough: The breed is named after Clydesdale, the valley of the River Clyde in Scotland where it was bred, so the clue is also a description.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a heavy draught horse breed, among the largest of working horses.

clue.text: German fellow with padded seat

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A German chap and his cushioned chair.
explanation.definitionFit: This low upholstered seat, often a footstool or box, has no back or arms.

clue.text: Mood fewer find unfunny in America

parts.note: humour can mean temperament or mood, as in 'in a good humour'; here in its American spelling
less means a smaller amount, fewer

explanation.surface: Someone with fewer moods who finds things dull, set in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In America' tells you to use the American spelling without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any sense of comedy, spelt the way US readers write it.

clue.text: Which PCs and surgeons have in common

definitions.text: Which PCs and surgeons have in common

parts.note: personal computers run software that controls the hardware
surgeons operate, so they too have a system for operating on patients

explanation.walkthrough: PCs could be police constables; the shared thing is the software of a computer and, punningly, the routine of an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the core software, such as Windows, that manages a computer's resources.

clue.text: Poet's a gangster

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ..., short for hoodlum, a criminal

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood wrote comic and protest verse such as 'The Song of the Shirt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood is slang for a hoodlum, a violent criminal, and is also the surname of the poet.

clue.text: Banner showing the Queen beside a brook

indicators.note: beside places the royal letters next to the watercourse, after it

parts.note: a brook is a small stream
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A flag displaying the monarch standing next to a little river.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant, as is a banner.

clue.text: Well off when the magician is with us

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest
taken as written

explanation.surface: We are rich whenever the sorcerer joins us.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wealthy and successful is what being well off means.

clue.text: New directions indicating the better part of valour

indicators.note: new tells you to make a fresh arrangement of the letters of directions

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh instructions pointing towards wise caution.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb from Henry IV Part 1 is 'the better part of valour is discretion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff's proverb names prudence as the wiser side of courage, so the definition quotes it.

clue.text: Gradually wear away tunnel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to erode or weaken little by little
second meaning: to dig beneath, as sappers did under castle walls

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are verbs; the literal digging sense gave rise to the figurative weakening one.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means to dig a mine under something, figuratively to weaken it slowly.

clue.text: Not impressed by beat in nude dance

indicators.note: in puts the word for beat inside the rearranged letters
dance makes the letters of nude jig about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
to stamp is to beat the ground with the feet

explanation.surface: Someone unmoved by stomping in a naked dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not impressed' looks like unamused, but it means not marked with a stamp, as an envelope might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter lacking a postage stamp or mark is literally not impressed with one.

clue.text: Study some outsiders crowded together

parts.note: a den is a private room for study

indicators.note: outsiders are the letters on the outside, the first and last of some

parts.note: its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: Research into a few outcasts packed closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense means thickly packed, with parts close together.

clue.text: Remains of girdles

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests leftover underwear; 'remains' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for continuing to be present and a noun for old-fashioned corsets.

clue.text: Notice her with royalty, a fan

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
taken as written
ER, the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Spot her accompanied by royalty, an admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent or follower sticks to a cause, as a supporter does.

clue.text: Agents of change in a classy teetotal organisation

indicators.note: organisation means putting the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reformers within a smart abstinence society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' looks like a society, but it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalysts speed up chemical reactions, and figuratively are people or things that trigger transformation.

clue.text: Article dropped from earliest revision though perfectly clean

indicators.note: revision means the letters of earliest are revised into a new order
dropped from says the article is let fall out of the reworked word

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to lose one and then rearrange
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item cut from the earliest draft, despite being spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile means free from germs, completely aseptic.

clue.text: First woman in chair turned out to be one that was successful

indicators.note: in puts the first woman inside the reshuffled seat letters
turned out means the letters of chair are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: The first female chairperson proved to be a success.
explanation.definitionFit: An achiever is a person who has accomplished things, a success.

clue.text: Part of another bold design for a plant

indicators.note: part of says the word lies within the letters of the following words

parts.note: the plant sits across the end of another and the start of bold

explanation.surface: A section of a striking pattern used for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb is a plant valued for flavour, scent or medicine.

clue.text: Some lab analyses showed nothing extraordinary

indicators.note: some says only a portion of the letters running through these words is used

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of lab into analyses

explanation.surface: A few laboratory tests revealed nothing unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means commonplace and trite, lacking anything remarkable.

clue.text: Sing out and gesture

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Singing loudly while waving a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing out' reads as one phrasal verb, but out is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a movement or signal conveying meaning, like a gesture.

clue.text: A chat up, or a long story

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
gas is informal for idle talk or a chat

explanation.surface: A flirtatious conversation, or else a lengthy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chat up' reads as flirting, but up is a signal for reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally an Old Norse epic tale.

clue.text: Fiction about a character, one previously giving human qualities to things

indicators.note: previously places the character and one ahead of the rest

parts.note: a character in a story is a person
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: about means the word Fiction goes round the letter a

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novel about a figure whose earlier role gave human traits to objects.
explanation.definitionFit: This figure of speech attributes human nature to inanimate objects or abstractions.

clue.text: Rushes to the game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: moves suddenly and quickly
second meaning: the pub game of throwing small missiles at a board

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone hurrying to a match; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for dashing and the name of the pub game played with a dartboard.

clue.text: No plainer version of the very best

indicators.note: a version is a new form, so the letters of no plainer are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: No simpler form exists of the finest example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil means having no equal, unrivalled, the finest of its kind.
